react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites converge on arachidonic acid metabolism as the primary perturbed pathway, confirmed across three independent analytical paradigms: multi-database over-representation analysis (RaMP), KEGG-specific pathway-set enrichment (MetaboAnalystR), and m/z-directed network activity profiling (Mummichog). RaMP returned WP:WP167 'Eicosanoid synthesis' as its top hit with an FDR of 9.7×10⁻¹⁴ and fold-enrichment of 1429, implicating five lipid mediators — arachidonic acid, 5(S)-HETE, 15(S)-HETE, leukotriene A4, and 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J2 — as the driver compounds. MetaboAnalystR independently identified KEGG:hsa00590 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' at rank 0 with four of the same metabolites (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE) hitting the 44-member pathway. Mummichog confirmed 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' as its rank-0 network hit (p=0.00067) with a 13/13 compound overlap including all five lipid drivers plus glycerol. Glycerol additionally anchored a secondary glycerophospholipid metabolism signal (Mummichog rank 1, p=0.009). 2-oxobutanoate (2-ketobutyric acid) independently mapped to KEGG valine, leucine, and isoleucine degradation (hsa00270) and propanoate metabolism (hsa00640) — consistent with pyruvate/ketobutyrate metabolic crosstalk. N-acetylgalactosamine and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid did not reach significance in the two ORA tools, representing peripheral or tissue-specific signals that do not converge on the eicosanoid core. The biological interpretation is a robust activation of the phospholipase-A2 → cyclooxygenase/lipoxygenase axis in the treatment condition, with arachidonic acid as the upstream substrate and the five detected eicosanoids as the downstream effectors of inflammation, cell signalling, and oxidative stress resolution.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Differentially abundant metabolites from the treatment group converge on the Eicosanoid synthesis pathway (WP:WP167) as the primary perturbed pathway, confirmed across the RaMP multi-database over-representation analysis (FDR = 9.7×10⁻¹⁴, rank 1) and mummichog m/z-directed profiling (p = 0.0013, rank 1). Five lipid mediators hit the 27-member WikiPathways Eicosanoid synthesis pathway: arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), 5(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04805), 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (KEGG:C14717). Mummichog confirmed these five driver compounds within the Arachidonic acid metabolism network (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, 13/13 overlap). Glycerol (KEGG:C00116) additionally participates in Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p = 0.009). 2-Ketobutyric acid (KEGG:C00109) was not detected as a significant pathway hit in either ORA tool, and N-acetylgalactosamine (KEGG:C01074) mapped only to sialic acid metabolism via mummichog.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Differentially abundant metabolites from the treatment group converge on the Eicosanoid synthesis pathway (WP:WP167) as the primary perturbed pathway, confirmed across the RaMP multi-database over-representation analysis (FDR = 9.7×10⁻¹⁴, rank 1) and mummichog m/z-directed profiling (p = 0.0013, rank 1). Five lipid mediators hit the 27-member WikiPathways Eicosanoid synthesis pathway: arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), 5(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04805), 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (KEGG:C14717). Mummichog confirmed these five driver compounds within the Arachidonic acid metabolism network (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, 13/13 overlap). Glycerol (KEGG:C00116) additionally participates in Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p = 0.009). 2-Ketobutyric acid (KEGG:C00109) was not detected as a significant pathway hit in either ORA tool, and N-acetylgalactosamine (KEGG:C01074) mapped only to sialic acid metabolism via mummichog.
